title: How Much Do Resellers Make a Year? Real Numbers for 2026
summary: Most resellers earn side income, but some are able to go full time. Here’s the real data on how much resellers make.
body_markdown:
There’s no official number for how much resellers make a year, and most people who resell do it to earn a little extra cash, not a full-time income. The typical online seller brings in about $100 a month in revenue, but some people do make a living reselling. Here’s what the data actually shows and how to estimate what you could make with reselling.


## Main Takeaways


- Income ranges from a little extra cash to a full-time living.
- The typical online seller brought in about $100 a month in revenue, before costs.
- In 2024, only 4% of US adults sold items they bought to resell, compared to 10% who sold their own used items.
- You can make a living reselling. 1 in 8 Whatnot sellers sell full-time, but most resellers treat it as side income.
- Your own income comes down to how many items you sell each week and how much profit you make on each one.
- Vendoo’s Profit Tracking and Business Analytics show what you really make across every marketplace, so you don’t have to guess.


## How Much Do Resellers Make a Year? The Honest Answer


There’s no official average for what resellers make in a year. Since there are different types of resellers, income can be a little extra cash or a full-time living. How much time you put in, your inventory opportunities, and how much you actually sell will determine your own earnings.


### **What the Data Shows**


Source What it measured Finding


Federal Reserve US adults who made money selling items in 2024 13% sold items. 4% sold things they bought to resell, while 10% sold their own used items


JPMorgan Chase Institute (2018 to 2021) Payments from online selling platforms into Chase bank accounts The typical seller brought in about $100 a month in revenue, before any expenses


Etsy Seller Census (2024) Survey of Etsy sellers (handmade, vintage and craft supplies, not only resellers) 30% of US sellers say their creative business is their only job, and it brings in 11% of household income on average


Omnisend (March 2026) Survey of 1,370 US adults about side hustles 32% of ecommerce side hustlers earn over $1,000 a month


Whatnot (2026) Whatnot’s own report on its live sellers 1 in 8 sellers have gone full-time


### **Most Resellers Sell Part Time**


For most people, reselling is side money, not a full-time income. The[JPMorgan Chase Institute](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/institute/all-topics/labor-markets-and-workforce/online-platform-economy-through-the-pandemic) found the typical person selling on online marketplaces brought in about $100 per month in revenue. The[Federal Reserve’s numbers](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2025-economic-well-being-of-us-households-in-2024-employment-and-gig-work.htm) showed something similar: 13% of US adults made money selling items, but most of them were cleaning out their closets, not running a business. Only 4% sold items they bought specifically to resell.


## How to Estimate Your Own Reselling Income


The easiest way to figure out how much you could make reselling in a year is to work the numbers out from how many items you sell and how much you keep on each one. Here’s a simple formula for you:


**Items sold per week × average profit per item × 52 weeks**


Some examples based on different types of resellers:


Seller type Items sold per week Average profit per item Yearly profit Monthly


Side hustler 5 $20 $5,200 $433


Part time 20 $20 $20,800 $1,733


Full time 50 $20 $52,000 $4,333


Keep in mind these numbers are before taxes and other costs like supplies, mileage, etc. so the real take-home would be lower. If you want to run your own numbers, you can plug your costs, sale price, and fees into our[profit margin calculator](https://vendoo.co/profit-margin-calculator) .


💡 **Tip:** Vendoo analytics track your sales and profit across every marketplace, so you can see your real numbers in any time period instead of guessing.


## What Affects How Much Resellers Make


How much you personally make comes down to a few things: mostly how much time you put in and what you pay for what you sell. Here’s what makes the biggest difference:


- **Hours you put in** : Sourcing, photos, listing, and shipping all take time. More listings usually mean more sales, but also more time. You don’t need to work full-time hours to make decent money, though. In an[Omnisend survey](https://www.omnisend.com/latest-news/32-of-ecommerce-side-hustlers-in-the-u-s-earn-1000-monthly-many-in-under-10-hours-a-week/) , 41% of side hustlers earning over $1,000 per month worked fewer than 10 hours per week.
- **What you pay for inventory** : Your profit relies heavily on what you paid for your items. A $3 thrift find that sells for $30 leaves much more room than a $15 find that sells for $30.
- **What you sell** : Some categories can bring higher profits than others while some have more competition and lower profits.
- **How many marketplaces you list on** : Each marketplace has its own buyers. An item that sits for a few weeks on one marketplace may sell quickly on another, so listing on multiple platforms gives your item more chances to sell.
- **Fees and shipping** : Since[fees and shipping costs](https://blog.vendoo.co/is-reselling-profitable) come out of every sale, paying attention to these is crucial to ensuring you’re making a profit.


## Can You Make a Living Reselling?


While some resellers do make a full-time living, most people treat reselling as a side income.


### **The Evidence**


There’s some real proof that people make it work full-time. In[Etsy’s 2024 Seller Census](https://storage.googleapis.com/etsy-extfiles-prod/2025_Q1_GLOBAL_Seller%20Census%202024.pdf) , 30% of US sellers said their creative business (on and off Etsy) is their only job. Those are mostly handmade and vintage sellers, not just resellers.


Live selling shows similar numbers.[One in eight Whatnot sellers](https://www.valueaddedresource.net/whatnot-2026-live-selling-report/) sell full-time on the platform.


### **What It Takes**


The resellers who make a living at this tend to do a few things consistently:


- **Source and list on a schedule:** Full-time income needs a steady flow of new inventory.
- **Track your numbers:** You need to know your real profit, not just your sales. A $3,000 month may look great until you consider inventory, fees, shipping and supplies.
- **Sell on more than one marketplace:** Listing items in more places puts them in front of more buyers, which helps you sell more without sourcing more. This is one of the best ways to save you time and money.


### **Taxes**


It’s important to remember that once reselling turns into a real income, taxes are involved.[The IRS says](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/understanding-your-form-1099-k) that a payment app or marketplace is required to send you a Form 1099-K if the payments you receive total more than $20,000 in more than 200 transactions. However, they may send you one with lower amounts or transactions. Not getting one doesn’t mean you’re off the hook. You still have to report your reselling income either way.


The key is to keep good records all year to make tax time easy. Our[bookkeeping for resellers](https://blog.vendoo.co/book-keeping-for-resellers) post walks you through a lot of the basics, but it’s always a good idea to talk to a tax professional who can give advice about your specific situation.

## Conclusion


So, how much do resellers make? For most people it’s side money, but the ones who treat reselling like a business can make a real living. Your numbers come down to how many items you sell and how much you profit on each one, so tracking your profit is the best way to know what you really make.


## FAQs


### **How much do resellers make a month?**


There’s no clean monthly average for resellers but a JPMorgan Chase Institute study found the typical online seller brought in about $100 a month in revenue, before costs. On the higher end, a 2026 Omnisend survey found 32% of US ecommerce side hustlers earn over $1,000 a month.


### **Can you make a living reselling?**


Yes, some people do, but most resellers treat it as side income. 30% of US Etsy sellers say their creative business is their only job, and 1 in 8 Whatnot sellers sell full-time.


### **How much do eBay resellers make?**


eBay doesn’t publish average seller earnings, so there’s no official number. A lot of eBay sellers aren’t full-time resellers. In eBay’s[2025 Recommerce Report](https://www.ebayinc.com/stories/news/2025-ebay-recommerce-report-publishes-today/) , 86% of eBay sellers source inventory from their own belongings.


### **Do resellers have to pay taxes?**


Yes. Reselling income has to be reported whether or not you get a Form 1099-K. Marketplaces have to send one once you go over $20,000 in more than 200 transactions, but they can send one for less.


### **How can I track how much I make reselling?**


A spreadsheet works, but it gets hard to keep up with as you grow. Vendoo’s Profit Tracking and Business Analytics use your cost of goods, sale price, marketplace fees, and shipping fees to calculate your profit and revenue, and you can see the totals by marketplace and date range.
